claims.text: On The Joe Rogan Experience #2264, appearing with Lenval Logan, Sands stated his service in his own words: 'I'm a retired master sergeant from the air Force. Worked 22 years, retired 2007. Started off as an airframe guy, ended up in intel.' A named man on a recording, self-reporting. The episode's publication date was not established from any page opened.

Brian Dunning, writing on 13 May 2024, gives an independent account of the same service: Air Force from 1985 to 2007, working in aircraft structural maintenance and then as an Electronic System Security Assessment specialist, retiring as a Master Sergeant, in a role involving 'collecting, analyzing, and processing Department of Defense telecommunications' and identifying 'critical information potentially compromised'. A named writer's dated account, not a personnel record.

claims.source: stated inference from the Joe Rogan Experience transcript and the Dunning piece
claims.text: The two accounts above agree on rank, on end date and on length of service, and 1985 to 2007 is 22 years. That is weak convergence on the service claim only, from two sources with no shared method, and it is not a service record. Nothing else about him converges at all.

The disputing material, from the same named critic on the same date. Brian Dunning itemises Sands's claims as including that the Wilson-Davis memo is genuine, which Dunning calls an 'obviously hoaxed' document; that alien spacecraft use electromagnetic propulsion; that aliens cooperated in reverse-engineering programmes; that a 'blue alien species' exists with whom humans can communicate telepathically; that non-physical aliens assist intelligence programmes; and that underground bases house aliens and that time travel and remote viewing are real. Dunning further states that Sands initially claimed involvement with the Navy's UAP Task Force and later contradicted himself, and that Sands has not run into any trouble violating DoD confidentiality protocols.

claims.source: stated inference; the committee witness lists were opened 2026-09-18 and do not name him
claims.text: The two attributes most often used to make Sands significant, that he appears in James Fox's documentary 'The Program' and that he gave testimony to Congress, the ICIG or AARO, are NOT established by any opened record. The film was not viewed and the one trade report on it was behind a paywall gateway. No congressional witness list names him. This claim exists to stop those attributes entering the board by repetition.

label: Jason Sands
narrative: Jason Sands is the thinnest node on this board and it is built deliberately thin. Not one primary record about him was opened: no personnel record, no filed document, no official mention. He is a real, distinct, identifiable person, because two independent openable artefacts converge on the same man with the same stated service history, and one of those two is a critic's. That is enough to justify a node under the same discipline that justified Brad Sorensen in the ARV thread, and it is not enough for a single Tier 1 claim. The node exists for two reasons. Its sceptical claim records a named critic's itemisation of what Sands asserts, which is the most substantive material about him in the open. And its last claim exists specifically to stop two attributes entering this board by repetition: that he appears in a named documentary, and that he has given testimony to Congress, the ICIG or AARO. Neither is established by any opened record.

sources.name: Brian Dunning, 'New UFO Whistleblower Jason Sands', a named critic's dated account and the source of both the service detail and the disputing material
